subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
unit: Unit 4: Service With a Smile (Listening & Speaking)
lesson: Role play, tour-guide problems and ‘The customer is always right’
outcomes: Suggest solutions using 'I think I would…'
Discuss whether 'the customer is always right'

tf.s: Harry Gordon Selfridge founded the store Selfridge's.
tf.why: Yes, and he is linked to the famous phrase.

tf.s: 'I think I would…' can introduce a hypothetical solution.
tf.why: Correct, it suggests what you would do.

tf.s: Workbook Activity 3 asks if the customer is right in different situations.
Some people criticise the phrase because some customers can be rude.
tf.why: Right, customers are not always right.

tf.s: A good waiter should argue loudly with an unhappy customer.
tf.why: A good waiter stays calm and polite.

tf.s: A hypothetical situation is one that has really happened.
In the role play, one person complains and the other responds politely.
tf.why: Yes, you practise complaining and responding.

tf.s: 'The best idea would be to…' is a phrase for complaining.
tf.why: It is a phrase for suggesting a solution.

tf.s: The customer is right in every situation, without exception.
tf.why: The lesson shows that sometimes the customer is wrong.

tf.s: The phrase encourages staff to give good service.
tf.why: Yes, that is one reason companies use it.

boxes.q: Who coined 'The customer is always right'?
boxes.why: Selfridge is linked to this phrase.

boxes.q: What could a waiter say to avoid a scene?
o: I'm sorry, let me fix that for you.
The best idea would be to…

boxes.q: What do groups do in Activity 5?
o: Choose a tour-guide problem and solve it
boxes.why: Groups decide what to do about a problem.

o: People who buy goods or services

boxes.why: In a role play you act a part.

boxes.q: What tone should staff use with a difficult customer?
Why do companies use the phrase?
boxes.why: It tells customers they will be treated well.

mcq.q: Which phrases introduce a hypothetical solution?
o: I think I would… / The best idea would be to…
Yesterday I went… / Last week I saw…
mcq.why: These phrases suggest what you would do.

mcq.q: Which store did Harry Gordon Selfridge found?
mcq.why: He was the founder of Selfridge's.

mcq.q: Which phrases do you use in the role play?
mcq.why: The Soundbites help you complain and reply.

o: A way to deal with a problem
mcq.why: Groups look for solutions to problems.

mcq.q: You are a waiter and a customer says the soup is cold. What do you say?
o: I'm so sorry. I'll bring you a hot one right away.

mcq.q: You are a tour guide and a tourist complains that the bus is late. Which response is best?
o: I'm sorry for the delay. The best idea would be to wait in the shade while I call the driver.
mcq.why: A polite response with a solution is best.

mcq.q: Complete: If a tourist lost his passport, I think I ___ help him call the embassy.
Why might the phrase make employees unhappy?
o: Staff must agree even when the customer is wrong or rude
mcq.why: Being told the customer is always right can feel unfair.

mcq.q: A customer shouts at a shop assistant for no reason. What is the best view?
o: The customer is not right, but the assistant should stay calm and polite
The customer is never wrong, so the assistant is to blame
The assistant should walk away and say nothing
mcq.why: Even when customers are wrong, good service stays polite.

mcq.q: Why is it good to stay polite with a difficult customer?
o: It calms the situation and protects the company's name
mcq.why: Politeness solves problems better than anger.
